scenario: Aug 30: The previously reviewed AP and Reuters reports describe progress on an Iran-Oman framework for a temporary Hormuz corridor and mine clearance after a tanker was disabled off Oman. Brent $88.10 (-0.47%), WTI $83.40 (-0.16%) and TTF $66.98 EUR/MWh (Aug 28; -1.89%); the JKM CFD reference remains carried at $21.22 and the $22.00 September-delivery assessment remains carried. Qatar LNG force majeure remains carried through mid-September. Crisis level remains 4 (High); base 10%, stress 60%, tail 30%.

categories.label: Food & Agriculture
categories.supplyChainImpact: Middle East fertilizer and energy exports remain constrained while Hormuz traffic stays near its reviewed low of about 13 vessel transits a day over the five days to Aug 11, far below the ~130/day pre-war norm (Kpler via Investing.com/Yahoo Finance, Aug 13; carried). Iran's parliament has now approved charging ships for Hormuz transit and Washington unveiled sweeping new sanctions, hardening the standoff before Oman's Tuesday visit, sustaining freight and input-cost risk for Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia planting chains while Qatar force majeure remains extended to mid-September.

categories.label: Petrochemicals & Plastics
categories.supplyChainImpact: SABIC, QAPCO and Omani exporters depend on Gulf shipping, while Southeast Asian crackers rely on Gulf condensate and naphtha. Hormuz traffic holds near its reviewed low of about 13 transits a day through Aug 11 (Kpler-sourced, carried), UKMTO still flags active mine danger areas, and Iran's newly approved transit-fee provision adds fresh compliance uncertainty for carriers. The hardened sanctions-and-fees standoff sustains combined feedstock, freight and delivery risk for plastics, packaging and agrochemicals.

assets.name: Naphtha (CFR Japan)
assets.narrative: Trading Economics printed the naphtha CFD reference at $747.24/mt on Aug 10 (+4.20% vs the prior close), tracking Brent's rally on Trump's reparations demand. A signed reopening would ease Gulf feedstock risk further; a collapsed deal would re-widen it. Source: Trading Economics, confirmed.

assets.name: Methanol (CFR China)
assets.narrative: The latest reviewed methanol observation remains $308/mt from Jul 24. Qatar force majeure and renewed Gulf attacks keep supply and freight risk elevated; no newer approved CFR China assessment is available. Source: Investing.com CFR China, carried.

categories.label: Fertilizers
categories.supplyChainImpact: The Strait of Hormuz remains the critical export artery for Middle East fertilizer supply. Qatar force majeure is extended to mid-September, and traffic stays near its reviewed low of about 13 transits a day through Aug 11, roughly 90% below pre-war norms (Kpler-sourced, carried). Iran's approved transit-fee provision and the newly unveiled US financial offensive keep delivery risk elevated across ASEAN planting chains pending a signed reopening.

Source: DTN/Argus Fertilizers, carried.

assets.narrative: The latest reviewed potash observation remains $418/mt from Jul 24. Renewed attacks and constrained Gulf traffic keep freight and insurance costs uncertain for ASEAN plantation inputs. Source: Argus Fertilizers/CRU, carried.

categories.label: Shipping & Freight
categories.supplyChainImpact: P&I war-risk constraints continue to divert or delay Gulf shipping as Washington's unveiled 'greatest financial offensive' sanctions meet Iran's newly approved transit-fee requirement, with the PGSA threatening fines, seizure or confiscation for rule-breaking vessels (CNBC/Anadolu, Aug 24). UKMTO reported no confirmed attacks over the 48 hours to Sunday but mine danger areas remain active, and reviewed Kpler data show transits near 13/day through Aug 11. Current route-normalised VLCC and LNG freight observations remain unavailable, so no verified cost uplift is published.

assets.name: Baltic Dry Index
assets.narrative: The latest reviewed BDI observation is 3,083 points from Aug 10 (Trading Economics), down 0.2% and roughly flat versus the Aug 7 print. It measures broad dry-bulk conditions and does not provide a route-normalised Hormuz freight cost. Source: Trading Economics, confirmed.

assets.name: VLCC AG-Asia Rate

Renewed attacks near Khasab and the prospect of a reopening keep the direction of risk two-sided. Source: Seatrade Maritime/Clarkson estimate.

assets.name: Container Freight (SCFI)
assets.narrative: The latest reviewed SCFI observation remains 1,480 points from Jul 24. It is a weekly container benchmark and does not establish current Gulf war-risk or rerouting costs. Source: Shanghai Shipping Exchange, carried.
